offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

findings.cause: ledger-consumer was recreated at 05:52:14Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Since then it books every copy of a provider event that reaches provider-events, without deduplicating on event_id. The provider resends webhooks, and webhook-receiver publishes each resend as its own Kafka message. So evt_000308 sat at three offsets on partition 0 and was posted three times, and evt_000251 sat at two offsets on partition 2 and was posted twice. All duplicate postings seen are from 05:52:15Z on, right after the recreation. Six duplicated payment.succeeded events inflate provider_clearing. One duplicated refund.succeeded (evt_000288, pay_000217, $24.55) leaves that payment's ledger balance at 1 cent against the provider's $24.56. Together these make the ledger +$493.23 ahead of the provider. The ledger stays internally balanced, and payments and refunds still match the provider, so only the ledger's posting is wrong. The alert is real.

evidence.shows: I confirmed the symptom with a settled money check. 7 events were posted more than once: evt_000308 three times, the others twice, including refund evt_000288. The ledger is +$493.23 against the provider. ledger_balanced, payments_match_provider and refunds_match_provider pass.
ledger-consumer is the only container recreated after the 05:50:43 stack start, at 05:52:14Z, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. payment-confirmer runs CONFIRMER_HANDLER=by_our_id.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 ($131.93) three times, at 05:52:28-30, from provider-events/0 offsets 100, 101 and 103, each with a different trace.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, at offsets 100, 101 and 103, with the same three trace ids. The duplicates are separate webhook deliveries, not a consumer replay of one offset.
ledger-consumer posted evt_000251 twice, at 05:52:15.133 and 05:52:15.757, from offsets 2＠73 and 2＠76, about 1s after the 05:52:14 recreation.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000251 twice, at offsets 73 and 76. The same pattern of redelivered copies, each booked by the ledger.

The ledger's 'already_processed' outcome falls from about 11/min to 2/min after 05:52, while 'posted' stays high. payment-confirmer keeps classifying most deliveries as already_confirmed or refund_already_confirmed, so the confirmer still deduplicates and the ledger mostly does not.

findings.left_open: I did not see the naive handler's code, so 'naive' meaning 'no event_id dedup' is inferred from its behavior and its name. proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 05:52:14Z deploy, using rollback_deploy. That should restore the event_id-deduplicating handler and stop new double postings. The wrong bookings need a separate data repair afterwards, which the rollback does not do. Then rerun the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Only ledger-consumer is touched. Its container is recreated, so ledger booking pauses briefly and Kafka lag builds, then drains. Payments, refunds and payment-confirmer are unaffected. Risk: the prior settings are not visible in the tool results. If the prior handler is not the deduplicating one, duplicates continue. Messages read again after the restart rely on that handler's dedup. Money already booked twice stays wrong until it is repaired.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If ledger-consumer misbehaves after the rollback (crash loop, stalled lag, new money-check failures), redeploy it with its current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) or stop it. Kafka holds the events, so stopping loses nothing. Booking resumes from committed offsets once a correct handler is in place.
